title: DualPrompt expert prompt bank with Mirror views
hypothesis: A shared expert-prompt basis plus one Mirror coordinate per task can preserve task-incremental output quality and old-task retention while using <=60% of independently stored expert prompts, on top of one common general prompt.
physical_object: One common frozen general prompt plus eight task-specific expert prompt vectors of length 64 decoded into 8x8 residual operators over frozen 8D features.
mirror_coordinate: One SO(2) Givens angle per task selects a functional expert prompt from a shared two-vector basis; the common general prompt is separate, identical and paid in every method.
logical_multiplicity: Eight task-specific expert prompt functions plus a common general prompt.
prior_art_delta: PA57 DualPrompt separates task-invariant general prompts from task-specific expert prompts. This task-incremental synthetic screen retains the common general prompt and tests compression/retention of expert values only.

model.prompt_decoder: reshape each length-64 prompt to an 8x8 linear residual map; fixed no-parameter synthetic decoder
model.task_identity: task ID is supplied at evaluation (task-incremental setting); retrieval is not part of this experiment.
methods: one common general prompt + eight independent expert prompts
one common general prompt + one hard-tied expert prompt
one common general prompt + one shared expert vector with task scalar gates
one common general prompt + shared 64x2 expert basis and two generic task coefficients
one common general prompt + shared 64x2 expert basis and one Givens Mirror angle per task
model.continual_schedule: Task order is fixed per world. Independent expert prompts train sequentially, one new prompt per task. The scalar expert vector trains on task 0 and is then frozen; later tasks train only their scalar. Generic and Mirror bases train jointly on tasks 0 and 1 for 1,200 updates, then freeze; tasks 2..7 train only their own new code for 1,200 updates. The hard-tied expert is updated sequentially on each task. Evaluate every seen task after each task stage to measure retention.

teacher.general_prompt: One deterministic world-specific frozen length-64 vector, shared and charged in every payload.
teacher.expert_prompts: Flattened B0 @ R(theta_i) @ A0 residual operators, where the eight task experts share a rank-2 basis and SO(2) angles. Deliberately aligned prompt-view feasibility fixture.
teacher.data: Per-task Gaussian frozen features; task target is common general-prompt output plus that task's expert-prompt residual output.

controls: independent expert prompt bank, mandatory full DualPrompt storage/quality control
shared expert vector plus scalar task gates
shared expert basis plus unrestricted two-value task coefficients
shared expert basis plus one Givens angle per task
common general prompt is identical and charged in every method

development.selection_metric: mean test output NRMSE on all seen tasks after each task stage; report per-task retention, old-task forgetting, total actual payload bytes and compute
development.allowed_tuning: No hyperparameter search planned. Task order and schedule are fixed in this protocol; any implementation correction reruns development only before fresh access.

fresh.open_gate: Both development worlds: independent mean expert NRMSE <=0.03; Mirror final mean test NRMSE <= independent +0.02 and <=0.10; Mirror old-task forgetting is no more than independent +0.01; Mirror complete payload <=0.60x independent; Mirror improves over scalar by >=0.01 at <=1.10x scalar bytes; unrestricted two-value coefficients do not match within 0.005 NRMSE at <=Mirror bytes. Otherwise fresh remains sealed.

storage.authority: actual serialized compressed NPZ inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: common general prompt in every method
all independent/shared expert prompt values or basis
every Mirror angle, scalar gate, or generic task coefficient
dimensions, task map, decoder metadata and NPZ names/headers/compression overhead

success_gate: All three fresh worlds pass final quality, old-task retention, <=60% complete payload, scalar and generic-coordinate comparisons with exact serialized replay.
failure_gate: Mirror misses task quality, retention or <=60% payload gate, scalar gate matches at comparable bytes, or generic coefficients match within 0.005 NRMSE at no greater bytes.
boundaries: synthetic frozen-feature task-incremental prompt screen, not a pretrained DualPrompt reproduction
the general prompt is fixed/shared; only expert-prompt compression is tested
task ID is supplied, so no task-free retrieval claim is made
expert task functions are deliberately generated on the same SO(2) orbit as Mirror
fixed training budgets do not establish near-converged capacity
